ledger.sentence: Osmotic laxatives hold water in the bowel to soften stools, and lactulose is the member covered on this site.
Local NHS guidance describes osmotic laxatives as retaining water, which increases stool volume and makes stools softer and easier to pass.
ledger.note: Search summary of local NHS laxative guidelines

ledger.sentence: The NHS says lactulose draws water into the bowel, which makes poo softer.
The NHS lists a past allergic reaction to lactulose, galactosaemia, lactose intolerance and galactose or fructose allergies as reasons to avoid it.
Irritable bowel syndrome, diverticular disease, Crohn's disease and a bowel blockage not caused by constipation are conditions where the NHS advises checking first.
The NHS says high amounts taken for many months might affect blood sugar in people with diabetes.
Diarrhoea, bloating and wind are common with lactulose, according to the NHS.
